blocks.prompt: 13 (i) There are 6 men and 8 women members of a club. how many committees of seven can be formed? (i) 3 women
blocks.explanation:
A committee of 7 with exactly 3 women, so the other \(7 - 3 = 4\) are men.
We must count such committees; order does not matter.
Plan: \({}^{8}C_{3} \times {}^{6}C_{4}\).
steps:
Given: 6 men, 8 women; committee of 7 with 3 women.
To find: the number of committees.
Method: 3 women from 8 and 4 men from 6, chosen together, so multiply the two combinations.

Choose the women
\[{}^{8}C_{3} = \dfrac{8 \cdot 7 \cdot 6}{3 \cdot 2 \cdot 1} = 56\]
Why: 3 women out of 8.

Choose the men
\[{}^{6}C_{4} = {}^{6}C_{2} = \dfrac{6 \cdot 5}{2} = 15\]
Why: The remaining 4 places go to men; choosing 4 of 6 equals leaving out 2 of 6.

Multiply
\[56 \times 15 = 840\]
Why: Each choice of women goes with each choice of men.

Check
\[3 + 4 = 7 \text{ members}\]
\[840 \div 15 = 56 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The committee size is right and the product divides back correctly.

blocks.prompt: 13 (ii) There are 6 men and 8 women members of a club. how many committees of seven can be formed? (ii) at the most 3 women
blocks.explanation:
"At the most 3 women" means 0, 1, 2 or 3 women; the men fill the rest of the 7 places.
We must add the committees of all allowed cases.
Plan: for each case multiply \({}^{8}C_{w} \times {}^{6}C_{7-w}\), then add.
steps:
Given: 6 men, 8 women; committee of 7 with at most 3 women.
To find: the number of committees.
Method: List the cases (number of women \(w\)). The cases cannot happen together, so add them.

Case \(w = 0\): 7 men
\[{}^{6}C_{7} = 0\]
Why: There are only 6 men, so a committee of 7 men is impossible.

Case \(w = 1\): 1 woman, 6 men
\[{}^{8}C_{1} \times {}^{6}C_{6} = 8 \times 1 = 8\]
Why: All 6 men must be taken (1 way).

Case \(w = 3\): 3 women, 4 men
\[{}^{8}C_{3} \times {}^{6}C_{4} = 56 \times 15 = 840\]
Why: This is part (i).

Add the cases
\[0 + 8 + 168 + 840 = 1016\]
Why: "At the most" joins the cases with OR, so we add.

Check
\[\text{all committees} = {}^{14}C_{7} = 3432\]
\[\text{4 or more women} = 1400 + 840 + 168 + 8 = 2416\]
\[1016 + 2416 = 3432 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Every committee has either at most 3 women or at least 4.

blocks.prompt: 13 (iii) There are 6 men and 8 women members of a club. how many committees of seven can be formed? (iii) at least 5 women?
blocks.explanation:
"At least 5 women" means 5, 6 or 7 women; men fill the rest.
We must add the committees of these cases.
Plan: \({}^{8}C_{w} \times {}^{6}C_{7-w}\) for \(w = 5, 6, 7\), then add.
steps:
Given: 6 men, 8 women; committee of 7 with at least 5 women.
To find: the number of committees.
Method: List the cases \(w = 5, 6, 7\) and add (a committee falls in only one case).

Case \(w = 7\): 7 women, no man
\[{}^{8}C_{7} \times {}^{6}C_{0} = 8 \times 1 = 8\]
Why: \({}^{8}C_{7} = {}^{8}C_{1} = 8\) and \({}^{6}C_{0} = 1\). This case is possible because there are 8 women.

Add the cases
\[840 + 168 + 8 = 1016\]
Why: "At least" joins the cases with OR, so we add.

Check
\[\text{at most 4 women} = 0 + 8 + 168 + 840 + 1400 = 2416\]
\[1016 + 2416 = 3432 = {}^{14}C_{7} \;\checkmark\]
Why: Committees with at least 5 women and with at most 4 women together make all committees.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: For part (iii) the answer key prints 1008. That is \(840 + 168\) only: it leaves out the committee of 7 women and no men (\({}^{8}C_{7} \times {}^{6}C_{0} = 8\)). The correct answer is \(840 + 168 + 8 = 1016\).
